sara: Quick RFC follow-up: we need a probe-driven staggered cutover plan for active-active write steering to avoid data residency violations.

amit: Good call. Can you outline the probe rules and rollback criteria? we had issues last time when a region flapped.

sara: Plan outline: maintain resident-region weight=100% until a probe success window of 5m for latency (p95 < 120ms), error_rate < 0.5%, and consent present. After window passes, ramp in 10% increments every 2m to the target weight. Any probe failure causes immediate rollback to resident-only.

marco: Should probes be per-tenant? that's expensive. Maybe per-region aggregated probes with sampled tenants, plus per-tenant for high-risk accounts.

linda: Also ensure session affinity is preserved for in-flight requests. runtime should pin session_id -> route for the life of the request and for N seconds after (session_pin_ttl_s = 30).

amit: Add a transient header when routing writes to non-resident regions: `x-residency-proxy: true` so storage layer can decide to do async replication or stronger syncing.

sara: Config snippet to land in routing-service:

```
{"probe_window_s":"300",
 "ramp_step_pct":"10",
 "ramp_interval_s":"120",
 "session_pin_ttl_s":"30",
 "consent_claim":"residency_consent",
 "fallback":"resident-only"}
```

linda: Mobile clients sometimes strip headers. rely on token claim `residency_consent` for enforcement.

qa-bot: note: add an integration test that injects a latency spike during ramp and asserts rollback within 60s.

marco: Ops runbook: manual console override only (no CLI toggles), alert on 2 consecutive probe failures in 10m, and automatic weight reset on rollback.

sara: rollout plan: staging smoke today, 10-tenant canary tomorrow, broader roll next week pending green.

amit: I'll own the telemetry dashboards for probe_result and ramp_events.

sara: Thanks. I'll update the RFC follow-up doc and create tickets for tests + runbook.
